_why: Destin, 2026-09-24 after appearance-panel-review-7: 'improve the actual theme cards themselves' — shape, style and preview; the only card action is the favourite star, always shown, 'kinda in style of resume browser tag/complete icons'. Three styles drawn by the real panel in the workbench.
title: Theme cards — three designs

steps.headline: Which theme card should the Themes box use?
steps.notice: In all three, the star is always shown as a small bare icon like the tag and complete icons in the session browser, so it works on touch screens too. Tap it to add or remove a favourite. Themes you built yourself also keep the pencil beside it, because that is the only way into their editor. The active theme gets an accent outline and a small 'Active' label.
steps.risk: The full theme names are only truncated when very long; all the built-in and community names fit.

variants.label: Framed picture
variants.summary: The theme's preview picture sits inside the card as a small framed thumbnail, with the name, Active label and star on a line beneath it in the app's own colours. Tidy and consistent with the other cards in the app, and it still shows wallpapers.

variants.label: Live colours
variants.summary: No picture: a tiny chat drawn live in the theme's own colours (header, your message, the reply, the message box). Always sharp and always matches the theme exactly, even with no preview file.
variants.risk: Wallpapers aren't shown, so wallpaper themes like Meadow Mist look plainer than they are.

variants.label: Full picture
variants.summary: The preview fills the whole card, with the name in white over a dark fade at the bottom and the star in the top corner. The biggest, most visual picture of the theme.
variants.risk: The dark fade muddies light themes like Crème, and the star can land on busy parts of the picture.
